overlaps.why: 12 of the 13 lessons of the smaller were in the larger, and the larger named the smaller as the one to do first: one sequence with two tiers. The old id resolves through sequenceAliases.

Two questions over shared lessons: how a measurement is made and what it claims, and which instrument answers which question. 14 of 19 lessons are in both because they are the bridge between them. Folding the smaller into the larger would give a path of 41 lessons, longer than any sequence now; the two stay, each at most 36.

The Solar System's bodies and other stars' planets are different subjects with 11 shared lessons (transit, tides, spin) that belong in both. Each is a pathway for a different course unit (Solar System and the Sun; the exoplanet unit).
